author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows both veterinarian lists to one specialty through the address
summary: The veterinarian directory page and the reinstated machine-readable veterinarian list each accept an optional specialty in the request address and show only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, ignoring case. A blank name leaves the list whole. The page offers no control for the filter.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-001] GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only the veterinarians holding the specialty whose whole name equals <name>, ignoring letter case (e.g. radiology, RADIOLOGY, Radiology all match radiology).

[REQ-VET-001] With a specialty named, pagination applies to the narrowed list, and every page link on the page (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carries the specialty parameter so filtered pages stay navigable.
[REQ-VET-001] A name that matches no veterinarian's specialty in full - an unknown name, or a prefix such as 'radio' - renders the normal directory page with an empty vet list, HTTP 200.
[REQ-VET-001] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value renders the same page as a request without the parameter.
[REQ-VET-001] A veterinarian in a narrowed list is shown with every specialty they hold, not only the one named (PRD Veterinarian directory edge case 3).
[REQ-VET-003] GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns the normal JSON document holding only the veterinarians holding that specialty, matched on the whole name ignoring letter case.
[REQ-VET-003] A name that matches no veterinarian's specialty in full returns the normal JSON document with an empty vet list, HTTP 200.
[REQ-VET-003] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value returns every veterinarian, as without the parameter.
[REQ-VET-001] [REQ-VET-003] Without the specialty parameter, /vets.html and /vets behave exactly as today (existing tests showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList keep passing).
non_goals: Any form, dropdown, link, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface; a follow-up request may add one (owner decision, intake line 1).
Any visible indication on the page that the list is narrowed; no new user-facing wording.
Free-text veterinarian search, and narrowing by a veterinarian's name (NG-9 as narrowed; the name question is recorded as a PRD open question).
Narrowing by more than one specialty in one request.
Trimming surrounding spaces from a non-blank specialty name (recorded as a PRD open question; only blank values are normalized).
notes: Owner decisions from intake line 1 and where each is recorded. Decision 1 narrows NG-9: the row is changed, the preamble names it decided, and non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-12-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md records the change. Decision 2 reinstates the JSON list as the fresh requirement REQ-VET-003. The REQ-VET-002 Superseded entry now points to REQ-VET-003 and stays withdrawn. Veterinarian directory edge case 2 (the known defect) is retired in place, keeping its number. Decision 3 (URL contract only; page links carry the parameter) shapes the acceptance criteria and non_goals. The HTML filter lands under REQ-VET-001 as new Done-when bullets rather than a second fresh REQ, which is the narrowest reading of 'Mint a fresh requirement for it'. Slice sizing: one code surface. Both lists share one matching rule, about 9 TDD cycles, batched because either half alone is 3-4 cycles over the same rule. For system-design-expert: system-design.md still calls the machine-readable route requirement-less and pending removal (Known Defects row, Contracts rows for Vets and VetController, overview 'no JSON API'). The PRD keeps the URL contract out of its prose, so the parameter name 'specialty' and both paths belong in Contracts. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new non-goal ADR, which is outside the product expert's write scope. Open questions added to the PRD: name filtering vs free-text search; padded specialty names.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The existing vet-list pattern handles this slice, with one parameter added to both surfaces. It follows the paged derived-query search that OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith demonstrates and the pagination helper already in VetController. Blank-value normalization is binding under architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog (Web controller row), so the controller holds no new business rule. The match rule lives in VetRepository as derived queries. No new module, type, or dependency. One sub-decision is new ground: the filtered reads are uncached (docs/adr/2026-09-12-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-bypass-the-cache.md). system-design.md now records the reinstated machine-readable list: Overview, the Contracts rows for Vets/VetRepository/VetController (REQ-VET-003 joined), a new 'Invariants of the specialty filter' paragraph, Security Context inputs/outputs, two Threat Model rows, the retired Known Defects row, and Open Question 5. Basis: grep and file reads of the vet package, OwnerController/OwnerRepository, the vet templates and the vendor schemas (IDE oracle not connected; the weaker basis).
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html and GET /vets: each handler binds an optional request-scoped String request parameter named specialty. No persisted type is bound, and the existing int page parameter is unchanged. A null, empty or whitespace-only value is normalized to 'no filter' in the handler (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row). A non-blank value passes to the repository unaltered, with no strip or case change (PRD non_goals: padded names are not trimmed).

Repository: two Spring Data derived queries on VetRepository match specialties.name with IgnoreCase and Distinct. One is paged (Pageable -> Page<Vet>) for /vets.html and one returns the whole collection for /vets. Neither carries @Cacheable (ADR 2026-09-12-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-bypass-the-cache). Unfiltered findAll() and findAll(Pageable) keep their cache unchanged.

Template, vetList.html: the handler exposes the normalized specialty (absent when no filter applies) to the model. Every page link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) is built with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}. specialty is emitted only when a filter applies, so unfiltered links render exactly as today. The request-derived value never goes inside __...__ preprocessing or string-concatenated URL text (system-design.md § Threat Model, echoed-specialty row).
Machine-readable list, GET /vets: returns the existing Vets wrapper holding the filtered collection. No paging (PRD non_goals).

Double at the repository boundary in VetControllerTests: keep the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository framework stub. The test's subject is web adaptation: binding, blank normalization, delegation, model attributes, page links and JSON shape. A hand-written double would re-implement the query's match rule, and a real repository needs the JPA slice that @WebMvcTest excludes. Stubs assert the name reaches the repository verbatim (e.g. 'RADIOLOGY') and that a blank value takes the unfiltered read. Paging is asserted with a PageImpl whose total exceeds one page.

Real repository, no double, for the match rule: add tests to ClinicServiceTests, the existing @DataJpaTest seam over real H2 seed data that already holds shouldFindVets. They must prove: whole name in any letter case ('RADIOLOGY' -> Helen Leary, Henry Stevens); the prefix 'radio' -> empty; 'surgery' -> Linda Douglas still holding dentistry and surgery; and the paged variant. The PRD's test_names stay in VetControllerTests; these repository tests are additional. Name them per docs/testing-principles.md.
Transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-layer harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).

patterns.description: paged Spring Data derived query taking a search value and a Pageable; model for the paged specialty read
blank search value normalized to the broadest search at binding; the specialty filter normalizes blank to no filter but does not strip non-blank values
existing pagination helper and model attributes the filtered page reuses
page links to convert to link-expression parameters; owners/ownersList.html links do not carry lastName and are no precedent for carrying a filter

risks.risk: A JOIN FETCH (or @EntityGraph) on the filter join loads only the named specialty into each vet, which breaks PRD edge case 3.
risks.mitigation: Use derived queries, so the filter join stays apart from the eager specialties collection; the ClinicServiceTests 'surgery' case proves it (system-design.md § Contracts, Invariants of the specialty filter).

risks.risk: Specialty names are not unique in any vendor schema, and H2's vet_specialties has no unique pair. A join can return a vet twice, and paging counts go wrong.
risks.mitigation: Distinct on both derived queries; Spring Data derives a count(distinct) for the paged count (system-design.md § Persistence: vendor schemas differ in constraints).

risks.risk: Folding case through column collation would repeat the PostgreSQL owner-search defect on a second surface.
risks.mitigation: IgnoreCase in the derived query folds case in the query itself on every vendor (system-design.md § Known Defects, first row; Invariants of the specialty filter).

risks.risk: Thymeleaf renders a null link parameter as a bare '?specialty' name, which changes unfiltered page links.
risks.mitigation: Emit the parameter only when a filter applies; existing showVetListHtml plus a link assertion on the unfiltered page guard 'behaves exactly as today'.

risks.risk: The request-derived specialty is echoed into href attributes. Concatenation allows parameter injection; __...__ preprocessing allows template expression injection.
risks.mitigation: Link-expression parameters only; output escaping stays on (security-principles.md § Realization, Cross-site scripting row; § Trust Boundaries, external input row; system-design.md § Threat Model).

risks.risk: Caching filtered reads keys an unbounded cache (no size limit or expiry in CacheConfiguration) on caller text, so any caller can grow memory.
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on the filtered reads (ADR 2026-09-12-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-bypass-the-cache; security-principles.md § Applying this section: no weaker than baseline).

notes: Autofix audit: the log holds no design-doc-autofix records. Hand-offs from the prd-entry notes are resolved in docs/system-design.md: the Known Defects row for the requirement-less route is removed; the Vets, VetRepository and VetController Contracts rows cite REQ-VET-003 and the VetController row names both paths and the specialty parameter; the Overview no longer implies the machine-readable list is unsupported; Security Context inputs and outputs are updated. docs/adr/README.md gains index rows for the product expert's non-goal ADR (not authored here) and the new cache ADR. The Thymeleaf ADR's 'one route departs from the pattern' remains accurate, so it is not superseded. Surface: no new endpoint. The parameter narrows an already public list and exposes nothing new (security-principles.md § Realization, widening-surface row). Open questions, recorded rather than awaited per the owner's statement: (1) Brief gap: security-principles.md § Realization has no row for resource exhaustion through request-keyed caches. The rule currently lives only in the new ADR, and writing the brief is outside this agent's write scope. (2) The paged unfiltered read is already keyed on an unclamped page number, a pre-existing exposure recorded in system-design.md Open Question 5 and outside this slice. (3) The Contracts preamble's precedent (WebConfiguration, CrashController) does not name routes. The VetController row names the paths and the parameter because the URL is the contract itself (intake decision 3); the doc-reviewer may weigh it. (4) Test placement extends the prd-entry file_targets with ClinicServiceTests.java: the match rule is a data-access property that a stubbed controller test cannot prove.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty value reaches the database only as a bound parameter of Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java:66 `Collection<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String name)` and :77 the Pageable overload); no query text is built from request input, and `grep -rn -F -e 'specialty' src/main/java/` found no other use of the value beyond VetController.java:48-91.

Template injection and link integrity: every page link carries the value as a Thymeleaf link-expression parameter (vetList.html `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`), which URL-encodes it; the change also removes the prior `__${i}__` preprocessing from all five links (diff lines 360, 375, 383, 391 show the removed `@{'/vets.html?page=__${...}__'}` forms). VetControllerTests `theVetDirectoryPageLinksShouldEncodeTheSpecialtyAsOneParameter` asserts `radiology&page=9` renders as `radiology%26page%3D9`, so a caller cannot smuggle extra parameters through the echo.

XSS: the request-supplied specialty is never rendered as text; it appears only inside th:href link parameters, and the specialty names shown come from the database through escaped `th:text="${specialty.name + ' '}"`. No th:utext or unescaped inlining was added (vetList.html read in full).

Mass assignment: the new input binds as a scalar `@RequestParam(required = false) String specialty` (VetController.java:48 and :74), not a @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody target, so no persisted type is bound from the request.

Cache growth: the filtered reads carry no @Cacheable (VetRepository.java diff lines 330-342 show only `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`), so caller-supplied text cannot add entries to the unbounded vets cache; the ADR 2026-09-12-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-bypass-the-cache records this, and the pre-existing unclamped page-number key stays recorded in system-design.md Open Questions item 5 rather than being extended.

Blank-value normalization is binding-layer shape normalization (VetController.java:91 `Optional.ofNullable(specialty).filter(name -> !name.isBlank())`), consistent with architecture-principles.md:85 and the owner search's null/strip handling at OwnerController.java:99-103; no validation, escaping call, or auth control was removed or weakened in the diff.

Exposed surface: no new endpoint; `/vets` and `/vets.html` pre-exist and gain one optional read-only parameter, and the threat model (system-design.md Security Context inputs and two new Threat Model rows) states the new input and its controls. No logging, no file I/O, no process execution, and no credentials were added in the diff (full diff read).

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set; `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` resolved Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5, and Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, with no jackson-dataformat-xml on the runtime classpath; dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured, so no NVD match ran in this review.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The `${specialty != null} ? @{...(...,specialty=${specialty})} : @{...(...)}` ternary is repeated verbatim at all five page-link sites (numbered link, first, previous, next, last). This is the exact duplication the checklist calls out: 'A conditional repeated across sibling sites (code, template elements, links) is duplication: compute it once (th:with or a fragment) and reference it.' Each site currently re-derives whether a filter is active instead of computing it once.
findings.fix: Hoist the specialty presence check to one place shared by all five links, e.g. `th:with="hasSpecialty=${specialty != null}"` on the enclosing `<div>`, and reference `${hasSpecialty}` in each ternary (or extract a `th:fragment` for one page link parameterized by page number, called five times). Either removes the five-way duplication of the same conditional.

./gradlew checkFormat passes cleanly on the fix delta.

The fix delta touches only the two files named in the open findings (docs/adr/2026-09-12-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md, src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html), per scripts/changeset.sh --base-tree 429b8dcd20eb44cd1dcc5512c334cf3be9bd1cec --name-only, so no new production behavior was introduced outside the reviewed surface.

author: change-grader
summary: filter both vet lists by specialty

blast_radius.note: Three production files in the vet feature package (VetController, VetRepository, vetList.html) plus docs; no sensitive paths, and the unfiltered read paths and their @Cacheable reads are untouched. The controller and template are a security surface because request text is written back into page links, but the reach is one feature.

semantic_surprise.note: The diff does what it says. A blank value falls back to the unchanged cached findAll, a non-blank value goes to derived IgnoreCase equality queries (whole name, not prefix), and unfiltered links render byte-identical hrefs. The fix-round th:with hoist is equivalent to the round-1 ternaries. One latent hazard: the new String model attribute 'specialty' shares its name with the th:each loop variable at vetList.html:20. That works because Thymeleaf locals are element-scoped, and a test renders both, but a later template edit could trip on it.

test_adequacy.note: The repository tests run against real H2 and cover letter case, prefix rejection, keeping every specialty, paging, and distinct listing and counting when two specialties share a name. The controller tests cover both surfaces, three blank variants, empty results, page-index mapping, links keeping or omitting the filter (the not-contains checks cover all five link kinds), and URL-encoding of 'radiology&page=9'. A broken implementation would fail these.

reviewer_hedging.note: Every final approval is clean and has no recommendations. Security and test approved in the full-battery round and were expected to sit out the fix-delta round. The one hedge: the doc-reviewer's round-1 check that the system-design prose matches the code cites VetRepository.java:317-343, which does not exist in the 82-line file (they are diff offsets). The claim itself is true: the findDistinct methods at lines 69 and 80 carry no @Cacheable. The unconfigured dependency check is a standing project gap, not a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: The change stays on the intake's surface. It adds the specialty parameter on /vets.html and /vets, whole-name case-insensitive matching, empty-list 200 responses, blank treated as absent, page links carrying the filter, and no UI control. It records the NG-9 narrowing ADR, mints REQ-VET-003 without reusing REQ-VET-002, and logs open questions. It had 0 design revisions and 0 consultations; the single build retry was a planned partial checkpoint, and the fix delta changed no behavior.

rationale: The code reads clean and is well tested. The only flag is the evidence behind one reviewer's check: the doc-reviewer cited a line range that does not exist in VetRepository.java. The claim itself holds. Read the specialty-filter paragraph in system-design.md against VetRepository.java:57-80, and note the 'specialty' name shared between the model attribute and the loop variable in vetList.html.
